label: Brief bytes cluster tightly: p10 244, p50 262, p90 298, max 361; 9 of 1,234 briefs (0.7 percent) are below 120 bytes, so head-only delivery almost never fires.
Reduced delivery requires a confirmed session id, a valid growing transcript and a stable clock; a new session, lifecycle boundary or changed directive set forces the full 219-byte block.
Because each behaviour-arm turn is a new session, the arm pays the directive on every prompt and 270.6 bytes is its per-prompt cost, not an upper bound.
A long-lived session would amortize to a 26-90 byte head, but no single-session multi-prompt record exists; five prompts sharing a session id with a growing transcript would confirm it.

direction: Treating 270.6 bytes as a per-session upper bound
reason: It is the per-prompt cost in a fresh-session population.
